name: Aimaq
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Efimov, Valentin A. 1997, Car-Ajmakov gruppa dialektov, in Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki; also Rastorgueva et al. 1997
earlier_scan.note: Russian dialectological chapter on Chahar Aimaq (Persian dialect cluster) plausibly states stress; not online

sources.citation: Kieffer, Charles M. 1983. Afghanistan v. Languages. Encyclopaedia Iranica I/5, 501-516 (online edition, iranicaonline.org/articles/afghanistan-v-languages).
sources.note: Only for Afghan Persian (Dari) dialects as a whole: 'The stress accent is less prominent than in Iranian speech but otherwise presents no remarkable characteristics.' Aymāq, Fīrūzkōhī and Taymanī speech are mentioned once, for three lexical items (šubuš 'louse', muṛče 'ant', ǰowz 'walnut') that place them in his 'Group B' (Khorasan-type) Persian dialects. No Aimaq-specific stress statement.

Bibliographic only: lists Kieffer 1983 and Ethnologue; no descriptive works. Glottolog's bibliography entry for the Jazyki mira chapter (Efimov 1997, pp. 230-232) is misattributed and mispaged, see Moshkalo 1997 above.
Nothing (same vowel/consonant content as the English article; no ударение).

sources.citation: Moshkalo, V. V. 1997. Čar-ajmakov gruppa dialektov [The Char-Aymak group of dialects]. In V. S. Rastorgueva, V. V. Moshkalo & D. I. Edel'man (eds.), Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki. I. Jugo-zapadnye iranskie jazyki, 200-202. Moskva: Indrik. (Glottolog lists this chapter as Efimov 1997, pp. 230-232; the printed table of contents and running heads give V. V. Moshkalo, pp. 200-202.)
sources.note: Nothing. The article covers names, ethnography, distribution and speaker numbers, then says (p. 201) that the Jamshidi, Taimani, Timuri and Firozkohi dialects have never been described, so no adequate linguistic description can be given; template sections 5 (phonetics/phonology) and 6 (grammar) read 'Сведений нет' (no information).

sources.citation: Janata, Alfred. 1987. Aymāq. Encyclopaedia Iranica III/2, 136-137 (online edition, iranicaonline.org/articles/aymaq).
sources.note: Nothing. Single sentence on language: 'The local dialects of the Aymāq are very close either to the Fārsī of east Khorasan province or to the Herātī idiom of Fārsī Darī.' Ethnographic and historical otherwise.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (English), 'Aimaq dialect', accessed 2026-09-17; cites Pisowicz 1985 (Origins of the New and Middle Persian phonological systems, pp. 112-114, 117) and Clifton 2005.
sources.note: Nothing; the phonology section lists vowel and consonant traits shared with eastern Persian (majhul vowels kept, /w/, /q/ vs /ɣ/) and does not mention stress. Secondary and uncited for the Aimaq-specific claims.

sources.citation: Windfuhr, Gernot & John R. Perry. 2009. Persian and Tajik. In Gernot Windfuhr (ed.), The Iranian Languages, 416-544. London: Routledge.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Modern English survey of Persian varieties including Afghan/Khorasani dialects; its stress section is for Persian generally and would only supply a family-level default, but it may cite any newer Aimaq-area work.

sources.citation: Kieffer, Charles M. (ed.). Atlas linguistique de l'Afghanistan (ALA) questionnaire materials for the Herat / Ghor Persian dialects (Aymāq, Fīrūzkōhī, Taymanī points), collected 1960s-70s; largely unpublished.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Kieffer 1983 says his 'Group B' classification of Aymāq/Fīrūzkōhī/Taymanī speech rests on ALA field points; the questionnaires would carry transcriptions with accent marks if any first-hand Aimaq stress data exist anywhere.

sources.citation: Efimov, V. A., V. S. Rastorgueva & E. N. Sharova. 1982. Persidskij, tadžikskij, dari. In V. S. Rastorgueva (ed.), Osnovy iranskogo jazykoznanija: Novoiranskie jazyki: zapadnaja gruppa, prikaspijskie jazyki, 5-230. Moskva: Nauka.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The fuller Soviet treatment of Dari and its Afghan dialects, written by the same circle (Efimov worked on Afghan Persian dialects); its Dari phonology gives a stress rule that may be stated to cover the western (Herat/Aimaq-area) dialects. Would at best give a Dari-level statement, not an Aimaq one.

sources.citation: Ferdinand, Klaus. 1964. Ethnographical notes on Chahār Aimāq, Hazāra and Moghōl. Acta Orientalia 28(1-2): 175-203.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Only other item in Glottolog's list that is about the Chahar Aimaq specifically; ethnographic, but Ferdinand recorded local vocabulary and may note pronunciation. Low odds of a stress statement.

sources.citation: Schurmann, H. F. 1962. The Mongols of Afghanistan: An Ethnography of the Moghôls and Related Peoples of Afghanistan. 's-Gravenhage: Mouton.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The one work Moshkalo 1997 cites for a linguistic judgment on the Aimaq dialects (Jamshidi and Firozkohi 'very similar'); it contains vocabularies and linguistic notes on the Chahar Aimaq and may mark accent in transcriptions. The only pre-1997 candidate for any first-hand phonetic remark.
